title: The $1 Raise That Costs You $3,200 in Benefits
hook: One extra dollar in income can legally cost you thousands in government benefits — and nobody warns you before you accept that promotion.
angle: The welfare cliff is a silent trap most finance content ignores: benefit programs have sharp income cutoffs where earning $1 more can erase thousands in annual subsidies. A raise can literally make you poorer — and 50M+ Americans are living near these cliffs without knowing it.
audience: Low-to-middle income earners ($40K–$70K single, up to $110K family) who receive ACA subsidies, Medicaid, SNAP, housing assistance, or childcare subsidies
key_numbers: Earning $1 above the ACA cliff at 400% FPL can cost $3,200+ in annual subsidies
The 400% FPL cliff for a single person is ~$58,320 in 2026
50+ million Americans live near at least one benefit cliff
Stacked benefit cliffs (health + food + housing + childcare) can total $12,500+ in losses
Only 1 in 4 workers knows their benefit cliff income level before negotiating
